the development of a framework and assessment on visual reasoning process adopted when integrating Cartesian graphs into mathematical problem solving on functions and derivatives among pre university students in Malaysia.

the use of graphs in teaching and learning of mathematical problems on functions, and their derivatives among pre university students, the development of a framework to describe and assess students' visual reasoning process in integrating Cartesian graphs in solving the mathematical problems, and the identification of the students' usage levels, preference method and graph reasoning ability when solving mathematical problems on Cartesian graphs.

the study provides a new insight into the visual reasoning process among Malaysian pre university students when relating algebraic forms of mathematical concepts and their derivatives to their Cartesian graphs and vice versa, and provides a new framework for visual reasoning in the teaching and leaning of mathematical concepts and derivatives.

visual reasoning is an important skill that is needed to be developed in students.
visual reasoning in solving mathematical problem on functions and derivatives is a complex process.

the use of graphs can enhance students' mathematical reasoning.
